title: LG, NVIDIA Expand Robotics Partnership
summary: LG and NVIDIA signed a memorandum of understanding on August 13, 2026 at NVIDIA's Santa Clara headquarters, with LG Corp chairman Kwang Mo Koo and NVIDIA CEO Jensen Huang in attendance. LG will build a next-generation bipedal humanoid robot powered by NVIDIA Jetson Thor for onboard compute, using NVIDIA Isaac GR00T as its foundation model and NVIDIA Halos for Robotics for safety, targeting a public unveiling in the first quarter of 2027. LG also plans to deploy its wheel-based CLOiD robot on a washing-machine production line in Tennessee this year for real-world validation, and to build a robot data pipeline using its LG CNS PhysicalWorks platform. The agreement separately covers an NVIDIA DSX/Vera Rubin-based AI factory reference site and a next-generation AI-defined vehicle platform on NVIDIA DRIVE Hyperion.
whyItMatters: The deal folds LG's manufacturing and component businesses -- actuators, sensors, batteries -- into NVIDIA's physical-AI stack, giving Isaac GR00T a large industrial partner willing to validate humanoids and wheeled robots on an active factory line rather than in a lab demo. It also shows how quickly "physical AI" partnerships are moving from roadmap talk to committed deployment dates, with a Tennessee production-line trial this year and a public robot reveal set for early 2027, a pattern other NVIDIA robotics partners are likely to follow.
